## Claim, scope and criteria

Test whether a configured first-five-kit workflow can carry a concern into an
accountable decision, implemented control and evidenced outcome. Criteria are the
original procedures in this folder, ORR-STD-DOC-001 r02 and the adopter's explicitly
configured duties. This protocol cannot establish four-standard conformity or
plant safety. The sample fictional case is explanatory, not test evidence.

## Assessor, sample and method

Appoint someone competent in the workflow and a relevant specialist for technical
criteria. Record name, competence, independence and conflicts; an author desk check
is not independent assurance. For a novice usability trial, observe an actual new
user completing the tasks with the supplied instructions; do not supply fabricated
participant answers as trial results.

For the pilot examine all five kit handoffs, one normal case, one missing-input
case, one failed control and one reopened decision. Record why that sample is
appropriate and its limits. For operations define a risk-based population and
period, select evidence across shifts/users and report sample size and omissions.
Document timestamps/freshness and uncertainty separately from pass/fail.

| Test | Method / evidence | Accept / hold rule |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | Trace party need to context source, boundary and unresolved duty owner | Hold if material exclusions/unknowns are concealed |
| ORCA chain | Follow objective → risk → discrete control → assurance across IDs | Fail if links missing or a control cannot be tested |
| Decision authority | Inspect delegation, exact decision and conditions | Pending if authority or competence absent |
| Measurement | Recalculate one result; try zero denominator and missing data | Unknown/not measurable, never automatic pass |
| Document release | Retrieve current instruction/form as an affected user on each sampled shift | Hold affected use if obsolete/inaccessible or briefing incomplete |
| Implementation vs outcome | Compare completion evidence with outcome criterion | outcome_pending until sufficient outcome evidence |
| Failure/reopening | Inject a missed execution and follow escalation, parent risk and action | Fail if original evidence disappears or issue is silently closed |
| Leadership | Trace an agenda item to decision, resources, owner, due date and next review | Hold unsupported conclusion; carry unresolved issue forward |
| Records | Retrieve origin/version; inspect one correction and recovery test evidence | Pending where protection/recovery remains untested |
| Usability | Observe novice execution; record confusion, help required and errors | Revise material ambiguities and retest affected steps |

## Recording, decision and follow-up

Retain an assessment record with ID, assessor/competence/independence, date/time
zone, exact document/configuration revisions or hashes, claim, criteria, population,
sample/selection rationale, evidence references, each result (Pass/Fail/Pending/N/A
with rationale), limitations/confidence, findings, owners/dates and retest criteria.
The authorized adopter records accept/hold for the exact scoped use; no empty cell
is a pass. Material failures hold the affected use/claim. Assign actions, preserve
the original result and record retest evidence before closure. Maintain assessment
records in the organization's private operational index under its appointed custodian.

Author checks of this draft concern content, links, fields and the fictional chain.
Independent review, real novice trial, actual approvals and operating effectiveness
remain pending. No certification outcome is predicted.

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.

r01 — 2026-11-01: initial original beginner-kit draft. Actual appointments,
competent review, representative user trial, approval and effectiveness pending.
Fictional decisions never authorize real work. Editable renditions, where supplied,
share this identity/revision; this Markdown is the master. Record a new derivative
identity/configuration when adapting, and reconcile changes before release.
